newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end down in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end down in dull trade.

text.p: Shenzhen B shares ended slightly down in dull trade on Monday as uncertainties over the annual results of B share firms persisted, dampening buying interest, brokers said.
The B share index shed 0.86 points or 0.53 percent to 160.41.
Turnover was HK$68.4 million, compared with Friday's HK$58.8 million.

"I don't expect any big movements in the market before the annual reporting season ends on April 30," one analyst said. Of the 44 Shenzhen-listed B share firms, only five have so far released their 1996 results.
"Investors are confident about China's economic outlook in 1997, which will prevent the index from falling sharply," the analyst said.
China's official securities newspapers on Monday warned of overheating on China's stock markets, which have seen gains of nearly 40 percent over the past three months.
But brokers said the warning was not a factor behind Monday's B share drop. "The warning is obviously aimed at the domestic A share markets," a trader with Shenzhen J&A Securities (HK) Ltd said.
Shenzhen's A share market, ignoring the warning, rose 4.97 points or 1.07 percent to 468.99, due to heavy buying in high-priced shares, brokers said.
Turnover was a massive 13.3 billion yuan against 12.4 billion the previous session.
On the B share market, black-and-white television tube maker Baoshi Electronics was the biggest loser, falling HK$0.32 or 6.68 percent to HK$4.47 on the heaviest trade of 1.87 million shares.
Brokers said investors were dumping Baoshi on talk that the company would post weak 1996 results.
